title: Theo and the Monsoon
premise: Theo Vasquez has spent years erasing themselves from their famous archaeologist father's shadow, digging alone in the river deltas where the law doesn't reach. When a dying prospector named Amara trades them a map to a sunken temple for a promise—deliver it to her daughter before the monsoon floods the valley forever—Theo is pulled into a race against rising water, rival treasure hunters, and their own buried grief. Alongside Jun, a boatman with his own reasons to distrust family legacies, Theo discovers the temple holds proof that their father stole his life's greatest find from Amara's expedition decades ago. In the climax, as the monsoon breaches the levees, Theo must choose between keeping the evidence and saving Jun's drowning village; they choose loyalty over truth's revenge, but deliver the map and let Amara's daughter decide what to do with it. The book ends with Theo, finally visible, standing at their father's door with the truth in hand—not to destroy him, but to be seen.
about_author: Coral Whitlock is a former river guide who spent six seasons navigating monsoon deltas before turning to fiction. She writes adventure stories about people who inherit more secrets than land.

chapters.title: The Weight of Water
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Working an illegal dig site in the delta lowlands, Theo unearths a shard bearing their father's excavation mark—and burns it rather than think about him. Establishes Theo's skill, isolation, and resentment. Emotional beat: controlled anger masking grief.

chapters.title: A Stranger's Last Bargain
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. A dying prospector, Amara, collapses at Theo's camp during pre-monsoon storms and offers a waterproofed map to a submerged temple in exchange for one promise: carry it to her daughter in Kessarin village before the rains seal the valley. Emotional beat: reluctant obligation taking root.

chapters.title: The Boatman Who Asks Nothing
chapters.summary: Jun's POV. Theo hires Jun, a taciturn boatman whose own family disowned him, to make the run upriver on a patched, leaking boat. Their wary negotiation establishes mutual terms: no questions, no names. Emotional beat: two guarded people testing trust.

chapters.title: What the River Keeps
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Navigating flooded channels, Theo deciphers the map's markings and recognizes survey techniques identical to their father's—impossible, since the site was never published. First hint of the connection. Emotional beat: unease sharpening into obsession.

chapters.title: Men With Clean Boots
chapters.summary: Jun's POV. Rival treasure hunters backed by a university charter—their father's institution—board the boat at a trading post, searching for 'stolen property.' Theo hides the map inside a false hull seam. Emotional beat: fear crystallizing into defiance.

chapters.title: Leaking Toward Kessarin
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The boat takes real damage running rapids ahead of the storm front; Jun reveals he grew up in Kessarin and was cast out for refusing to lie about a drowning. Theo shares nothing in return, and feels the cost of it. Emotional beat: intimacy through withheld wounds.

chapters.title: The Temple Under the Floodline
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Reaching the temple just as waters rise, Theo dives the flooded antechamber and finds Amara's original expedition journal—proving their father plagiarized her discovery and buried her career. Emotional beat: vindication curdling into horror.

chapters.title: The Levee Breaks
chapters.summary: Jun's POV. The monsoon hits full force; the Kessarin levee fails and the valley begins to drown, including the village where Amara's daughter waits. The hunters close in, and Theo must choose: save the journal or help evacuate. Emotional beat: crisis forcing values into the open.

chapters.title: Loyalty Is a Choice You Make Twice
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo abandons the journal to the flood, hauling villagers and Jun's estranged sister to high ground while the hunters' camp washes away. Amara's daughter receives only the map—and the story of her mother's promise kept. Emotional beat: grief transmuted into chosen loyalty.

chapters.title: Visible
chapters.summary: Theo's POV, epilogue weeks later. The flood recedes; Amara's daughter, using the map, raises a claim that forces the university to investigate. Theo travels to their father's door carrying not the journal but their own name spoken aloud. Emotional beat: quiet, hard-won reconciliation with being seen.
